findings.title: Frontmatter parser swallows read errors, and each file is read twice
findings.description: `validateFile` calls `parseFrontmatter(file)` and then `readFile(file)` again. `parseFrontmatter` (`frontmatterParser.ts:63-65`) catches every error and returns an empty result. If a read fails after `preflight` succeeds (file removed, permissions changed, EIO), the failure is reported as a missing `docType`. The user then sees "frontmatter must declare 'docType: slice-design'" for a file that was never read. The explicit `try/catch` around the second `readFile` is the only real guard, and it is unreachable in that scenario because the docType check returns first. This also violates the project rule against swallowing errors without a reason. Read the file once and derive the frontmatter from that text, or call `readFile` first and let its error propagate as `SliceDesignValidationError`. That removes the double I/O and the misleading failure.

findings.title: Usage and template errors have no machine-readable error code in `--json` mode
findings.description: The empty-file-list case and every error from core (missing template, no required headings, missing or unreadable file) throw `SliceDesignValidationError`, which extends `Error`, not the CLI's `UserError`. In `handleError` (`errors.ts:46-59`) this takes the generic `Error` branch. JSON consumers get `code: "UNKNOWN"` with no `suggestion`. The command's description promises "exit 2 usage or template error" as a contract. Other commands, such as `validateFrontmatterAction`, raise `UserError` with an `ErrorCode`. Catch `SliceDesignValidationError` in the CLI action and rethrow as `UserError` with an appropriate code, for example `INVALID_ARGUMENT` or `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`. The empty-args check in particular belongs in the CLI layer as a `UserError`, not a core error class.

findings.title: Project and worktree resolution duplicated from the frontmatter command
findings.description: `resolveTemplatePath` repeats the sequence in `validate.ts:154-166`: construct the store, call `resolveProjectWorktree`, call `getById`, throw "Project not found", then resolve the operation path. The two copies already differ: frontmatter falls back to `project.projectPath`, while design throws. A shared helper would keep the "not found" message and the worktree rules in one place.

findings.title: Fence detection only recognises column-0 triple-backtick fences
findings.description: `line.startsWith('```')` ignores `~~~` fences and fences indented inside list items. It also toggles on any backtick line regardless of the opening fence length. Headings inside such blocks are counted as real, so a design could pass with a required heading that exists only in an example block. This matches the ported bash script, so it is not a regression. It does conflict with the project's "lenient parsing" guidance, and a short test would document the limits.

findings.title: Parameter mutability annotations are inconsistent
findings.description: The TypeScript rules ask for `readonly` on parameters that are not mutated. `preflight` and `validateSliceDesignFiles` take `readonly string[]`. `missingHeadings(required, docKeys)` and `validateFile(..., required: RequiredHeading[])` take mutable arrays and never mutate them.

findings.title: Tests are coupled to live repository documents
findings.description: The tests hard-code slices 212, 213, 214 and 928 and the installed guide template. This follows the project's real-input fixture rule and is valuable. But an unrelated edit to one of those designs, or a guide update that adds a required heading, will fail these tests for reasons unrelated to the validator. Keep the 214 design as the single real-world anchor and use synthetic fixtures elsewhere, or add a comment saying the dependency is intentional.

findings.title: Layering, exports and test coverage
findings.description: The pure validator is exported from the browser-safe `index.ts`. The fs-dependent layer is exported from `node.ts`. `SLICE_DESIGN_TEMPLATE_RELATIVE_PATH` reaches `@context-forge/core/node` through `guides/index.ts`, so the CLI imports resolve. Tests cover heading normalisation, CRLF, level mismatch, fences, docType failure, preflight all-or-nothing behaviour, exit codes with empty stdout in both output modes, and worktree-specific template resolution.
